summary: WebFetch successfully reached first-party pages this run (not blocked as the standard playbook assumes), so verification is based on direct reads, not search snippets alone. Re-checked all 45 rotation-batch providers via WebFetch: 40 confirmed active on their own pages (listed in checked_active). openmetal.io repeatedly returned truncated content and could not be confirmed; oracle.com/cloud, genesis-cloud, and dreamcompute's page returned blocked/inconclusive responses (403/503, or no mention of the named product) and are left unconfirmed rather than treated as evidence of any change. Two status alerts are raised, each backed by a first-party redirect plus corroborating reporting: fleek.xyz now 301s to fleek.sh, which shows only a vague relaunch placeholder, and hathora.dev now 301s to gamefabric.com following Hathora's acquisition by Fireworks AI and the wind-down of its game-hosting business. Two new candidates are proposed from discovery searches and confirmed by directly reading their official sites: SwiftWave (self-hosted open-source PaaS) and General Compute (ASIC-first inference cloud). No metadata updates were proposed because verified entries already matched the catalog (e.g. google-cloud-functions is already named 'Google Cloud Run functions').

new_candidates.name: SwiftWave
new_candidates.summary: A self-hosted, lightweight open-source PaaS for deploying apps from Git, Docker images, or source onto any server, with an app store and SSL automation.
new_candidates.best_for: Developers who want a Heroku/Vercel-like deploy experience on their own VPS or bare metal without vendor lock-in.
new_candidates.change_note: New candidate discovered via self-hosted-PaaS discovery search; confirmed active and open source by reading swiftwave.org and its GitHub repository (906 stars, active develop branch) directly.

new_candidates.name: General Compute
new_candidates.summary: An inference cloud running purpose-built accelerator silicon (SambaNova, Cerebras, Positron, d-Matrix) with a self-serve, OpenAI-compatible API aimed at low-latency agent workloads.
new_candidates.best_for: Teams needing sub-300ms time-to-first-token inference for agentic workloads without managing heterogeneous accelerator hardware themselves.
new_candidates.change_note: New candidate discovered via GPU/AI-cloud discovery search; confirmed active and described directly by reading the official generalcompute.com site, including its self-serve API and hardware model.

status_alerts.rationale: fleek.xyz now 301-redirects to fleek.sh, whose own page reads only 'We've been building something new. We're excited to share more soon' with no working hosting product visible. This first-party redirect/placeholder is corroborated by IPFS's own docs case study (docs.ipfs.tech/case-studies/fleek/), which states Fleek's IPFS hosting service was discontinued on January 31, 2026 and is 'preserved for historical purposes', and by the IPFS blog's 2026 Fleek migration post describing Fleek's pivot to AI and the resulting migration of hosted sites to other pinning providers.

hathora.dev (the catalog's canonical URL) now 301-redirects to gamefabric.com, with no trace of the original game-hosting product at that domain. This first-party redirect corroborates multiple reports (SiliconANGLE, PCWorld, TechSpot) that Fireworks AI acquired Hathora around March 3-4, 2026 as a talent/infrastructure acquisition, froze new provisioning immediately, and fully shut down the game-hosting service on May 5, 2026, with customers transitioned to Nitrado via GameFabric.
